perspective: Adversarial verification of role-based visibility, edit authority, and sensitive-data boundaries across Mayra, Laura/HR, Finance/Daisy, faculty, students, Box, FAST, Oracle, and derived workflow proposals.

findings.claim: Finance reconciliation data is restricted to Finance; Mayra and Laura do not currently have access.
findings.risk: High: the proposed app cannot expose reconciliation, active-grant, startup, or distribution data to all users without violating the stated sensitivity boundary.
findings.recommendation: Make Finance data a separately authorized scope; default-deny Mayra/Laura and require explicit Finance grants for each sensitive dataset.

findings.claim: The proposal that everybody can see everything while only some users can edit conflicts with the interview-stated Finance restriction.
findings.risk: Critical: read access alone would disclose sensitive reconciliation, grant, salary-distribution, and startup information.
findings.recommendation: Reject universal visibility. Define field- and dataset-level read scopes before implementation; edit controls are insufficient.

findings.claim: Mayra owns intake/new-entry work, but should not edit Laura's HR/Oracle workflow statuses; Laura explicitly needs to see and act on those statuses.
findings.risk: High: unrestricted status editing could falsely signal screening, signature, Oracle entry, approval, or verification completion.
findings.recommendation: Permit Mayra to create/prepare intake and submit change requests; restrict Laura/authorized HR users to HR workflow and Oracle-status mutations; preserve append-only history.

findings.claim: Laura and an HR colleague currently share operational visibility and can perform overlapping HR tracking work, but the exact delegated edit boundary is not specified.
findings.risk: Medium: two-person collaboration without named permissions, actor attribution, or separation of duties weakens auditability.
findings.recommendation: Model named HR roles, record actor/time/reason for every transition, and specify whether the colleague may initiate screening, send DocuSign, enter Oracle, verify, or only assist.

findings.claim: Students' address, date of birth, gender, and phone are required for new-hire pending-worker processing, but transcript evidence does not establish who may view or edit those fields in the app.
findings.risk: Critical: unnecessary exposure of student PII to Mayra, Finance, faculty, or broad app users; unclear source-of-truth and correction authority.
findings.recommendation: Define least-privilege PII fields and masking, restrict raw PII to authorized HR/pending-worker handlers, and keep Finance/faculty views to required derived fields.

findings.claim: Oracle edit and verification authority is held by Laura/HR in the described workflow; Mayra expressly lacks Oracle access. Finance Oracle costing authority is described but not mapped to named users.
findings.risk: High: combining appointment edits, HR verification, and Finance costing could permit unauthorized payroll-impacting changes.
findings.recommendation: Separate appointment/HR mutations from Finance chartfield and costing mutations; document Oracle roles, approval gates, and whether app writes are authoritative or merely staging.

findings.claim: FAST/Box access and integration are not established as current system capabilities; Daisy identifies Finance-owned Box data and possible FAST retrieval, while integration is discussed as future work.
findings.risk: High: treating proposed connectors or shared folders as existing authorization could bypass Box/FAST controls or create unauthorized copies.
findings.recommendation: Do not claim or implement access until the data owner, connector identity, scopes, write/read direction, audit logging, and revocation process are approved.

findings.claim: Finance needs selected HR offer-letter/startup information, but the proposed attachment-sharing boundary is unresolved.
findings.risk: High: offer letters contain salary and startup-package details; broad attachment access would disclose sensitive faculty compensation and financial commitments.
findings.recommendation: Define a Finance-specific projection or redacted attachment view; do not expose whole HR folders or unrestricted offer-letter files.

findings.claim: Faculty/student requests may arrive through email, Teams, or directly to Laura/Daisy, but the stated operating rule is that Laura acts only on records in the spreadsheet/app; direct requester permissions are unresolved.
findings.risk: Medium: bypass channels can cause unauthorized or unaudited changes, while forcing faculty into a future form is explicitly not current policy.
findings.recommendation: Keep faculty as request submitters, not direct editors of authoritative appointment records; route requests to Mayra/authorized HR and retain source correspondence or structured attestations.

findings.claim: Mayra's confirmation is evidence for renewal/chartfield intent, but it is not established as authority to edit Finance reconciliation or approve payroll costing.
findings.risk: High: conflating intake confirmation with Finance approval could silently authorize wrong accounts or funded distributions.
findings.recommendation: Treat Mayra's entry/confirmation as intake provenance only; require Finance verification and explicit Finance mutation for chartfield, distribution, fringe, and costing fields.

findings.claim: Cross-domain reporting for tenure/promotion and workforce data is requested by Daisy, but the allowed audience and field-level visibility are not defined.
findings.risk: High: reports could expose faculty employment history, salary, status, or promotion data beyond business need.
findings.recommendation: Define report-specific audiences, row/column security, export restrictions, and whether historical HR data is visible to Finance, HR, faculty, or administrators.

findings.claim: The derived pipeline correctly identifies role owners for major steps, but it must not be treated as proof of complete authorization policy; several ownership claims are marked assumed or second-hand.
findings.risk: Medium: implementing permissions from provisional summaries could turn assumptions into production access rules.
findings.recommendation: Use transcripts as authority, preserve confirmed/assumed labels, and require owner approval for unresolved role, delegation, and system-access decisions.

missing_or_ambiguous: No authoritative role matrix names who may view/edit each field or dataset.
No confirmed app identity, authentication mechanism, group-to-role mapping, or revocation process.
No field-level classification for student PII, faculty compensation, startup packages, chartfields, distributions, or reconciliation data.
No proof that Box, FAST, Oracle, Banner, or the USF lookup site can be connected under approved service/user scopes.
No precise separation between staging edits in the app and authoritative writes in Oracle, FAST, Box, or Banner.
No exact Finance delegation: which Finance users can edit chartfields, distributions, statuses, active appointments, or Oracle costing.
No exact HR delegation for Laura's colleague or other HR users.
No policy for faculty/student visibility, direct editing, exports, downloads, email automation, or attachments.
No owner decision on whether Finance receives whole offer letters or only redacted/projection data.
No retention, audit-log immutability, correction, or break-glass access policy established in the evidence.
